# Transition grouping recovers encoded word sequences

<a id="主张-claim"></a>
## Claim

For every alphabet and every adjacency relation r: reading from the right, an element joins the following group where r links it to that group's first element and opens a new group otherwise; grouping returns a partition exactly when every group is nonempty, linked by r inside and not linked to the next, that partition is unique, and grouping never changes the sequence. For a vocabulary of nonempty words, grouping recovers the words of every encoded sequence exactly when each word is linked inside and the last element of no word is linked to the first element of any word — both local conditions on adjacent pairs. A relation learned as the strict majority of observed transitions links each element to at most one successor. The existing grouping algorithm and two-word encoding are these definitions: every two-word sequence is recovered exactly when a→b and c→d are linked and b→a, b→c, d→a, d→c are not; idealBond and the relation an encounter history actually acquires are instances.

Canonical source: [LearnedGrouping.lean](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/LearnedGrouping.lean)

<a id="前提与对应-hypotheses-and-correspondence"></a>
## Hypotheses and correspondence

- The general law places no condition on the alphabet or relation; the instance uses four elementary events, the two-word encoding and idealBond.
- The acquisition witness uses the stated encounter sequence, strict-majority criterion and adequate recording support.

The relation is a grouping criterion derived from observed transitions in a log; sound categories and linguistic correspondence are not derived.

<a id="检验与边界-validation-and-boundaries"></a>
## Validation and boundaries

Migrates the specified grouping result from the existing 23-theorem/51-audit package; registration adds no theorem or proof rerun.

The grouping rule is fixed; arbitrary-length correspondence does not guarantee affordable execution or establish natural language and complete cognition.

- Repetition can merge intended boundaries; partial experience can parse one expression while misgrouping another. [AcquiredSegmentation.lean](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/inquiry-root/AcquiredSegmentation.lean)
- A relation learned by strict majority is functional: where two words continue one element differently inside, no record of transitions groups both. [Segmentation.lean](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Segmentation.lean)
